#                   andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512, pairing the default vsim
#                   engine). Override together with VSIM_BIN to run a
#                   fixture on another engine, e.g. the S/U-capable
#                   ax66_makatau for the rt_priv_* fixtures (the default
#                   ax45mpv_premium RTL is M-mode-only).

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/roi.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-marker}"
QEMU_CPU="${QEMU_CPU:-andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512}"

hybrid_resolve_paths

NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"

case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
  marker) ;;
  pc)
    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
      exit 77
    fi
    # ROI_START / ROI_END name the two switch PCs (0x address or symbol in
    # $VSIM_ELF). ./andesim run always passes them explicitly. When a caller
    # leaves BOTH unset (e.g. the bulk runner scripts/run_e2e.sh), derive them
    # from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via objdump, so pc mode needs no
    # per-fixture config and no planted boundary symbols. A partial set or a
    # derivation miss falls through to roi_resolve_pair's required-vars error.
    if [ -z "${ROI_START:-}" ] && [ -z "${ROI_END:-}" ]; then
      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
      if command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
         && MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")"); then
        ROI_START="0x${MARKERS%% *}"
        ROI_END="0x${MARKERS##* }"
        export ROI_START ROI_END
      fi
    fi
    NM_OUT=$("$NM" --defined-only "$VSIM_ELF")
    roi_resolve_pair "$NM_OUT" "$FIXTURE pc" || exit 1
    ;;
  *)
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (use marker|pc)"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

# 128 MB program RAM matches the QEMU virt machine default. L26/F2: the
# physical mmap reserves one V-scratch page (HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES =
# 32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX) ABOVE the program's RAM, so the V-transport
# scratch (vsim parks it at the mmap top page) sits past anything the program
# can address. Mirrors the andesim driver (shm.cpp physical_mmap_bytes).
# Read HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX from the shared ABI so this tracks the header
# (the ceiling moved 64 -> 128 once already) instead of hardcoding it.
VLEN_BYTES_MAX=$(awk '/^#define HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX/ {print $3}' \
  "$SCRIPT_DIR/../include/hybrid/state_abi.h")
[ -n "$VLEN_BYTES_MAX" ] || { echo "e2e: cannot read HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX from state_abi.h" >&2; exit 1; }
PROGRAM_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
V_SCRATCH_BYTES=$((32 * VLEN_BYTES_MAX))
SHARED_SIZE=$((PROGRAM_SIZE + V_SCRATCH_BYTES))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)

findings.detail: tests/fixtures/runtime/platform.h (54 lines, include guard __AE350_H, 'Address mapping for AE350', a trap-context struct + AE350 MMIO addresses) is git-tracked but referenced by nothing. `grep -rn 'platform.h|__AE350_H'` across the whole main tree (all extensions, excluding .git and worktrees) matches only the file itself; the fixtures Makefile references only runtime/rt_c_helpers.h and runtime/memory_map.h (lines 168, 173-174, 179, 194, 200, 203, 224, 235). findings.title: rt_all_fprs fixture is built by `all` but never run by any harness
findings.detail: rt_all_fprs is in RT_FIXTURES (tests/fixtures/Makefile:30) so `make all` builds it, but it appears in NO runner: scripts/run_e2e.sh's REQUIRED_ELFS (line 63-69), RT_TESTS (83-108), and SERIAL_RT_TESTS (124-127) all omit it, and grep across tests/**/*.sh, scripts/, driver/, docs/ finds zero references (its sibling rt_all_gprs IS wired at run_e2e.sh:89). `git log --all -S rt_all_fprs` shows it was only ever consumed by docs/register_transport_tutorial.ipynb, which was deleted in 67ab27b ('docs: remove retired notebooks'). It never appeared in run_e2e.sh or tests/e2e.sh in any commit. Fix options: (a) wire it into RT_TESTS with one line 'rt_all_fprs|FIXTURE=rt_all_fprs' (restores FPR-sweep e2e coverage; the FPR abstract-command transport currently has no dedicated e2e test - rt_c_fcsr covers only fcsr), or (b) drop the fixture and its RT_FIXTURES entry. Option (a) looks intended given the sibling symmetry.
findings.safety: Option (a) only adds a test to the suite (fixture is self-verifying, exits 0 on pass, same harness contract as rt_all_gprs); option (b) removes a file nothing runs. Neither changes product behavior.

findings.title: REQUIRED_ELFS is a hand-copied subset of RT_TESTS and has drifted (6 fixtures missing)
findings.detail: REQUIRED_ELFS (lines 63-69) exists only to decide whether to run `make -C tests/fixtures` (lines 70-77), but it is a second hand-maintained copy of the fixture list and has drifted from RT_TESTS (83-108): rt_m_ext_counters, rt_m_ext_trigcause, rt_c_static_buf, rt_c_dlm_data, rt_c_ilm_code, and rt_c_hvm_data are run by RT_TESTS but absent from REQUIRED_ELFS. Structural fix: derive the list from RT_TESTS/SERIAL_RT_TESTS entries (parse the FIXTURE= token), or drop the check and always run `make -C "$TEST_DIR" -j` (idempotent no-op when up to date).
findings.safety: The list only gates a rebuild trigger; deriving it from RT_TESTS (or always invoking make) produces the same or a strictly-superset build set, so every test still finds its ELF and no test command changes.
